k: <1>Practise at home</1> until you can walk, sit and use the bathroom confidently — the number one first-timer anxiety. Safety pins on the izar are used by many pilgrims; scholars differ, so a belt is the cleanest option.

<1>Prayers:</1> sit when you must; combine where the sunnah combines (Arafah, Muzdalifah); shorten in Mina if your school counts you a traveller (Hanafis after {1}+ days in Makkah pray four; so do Shafi'is after {2} full days there, not counting the days of arrival and departure, if they will also stay on {3} full days after the Hajj, and Hanbalis if they will stay on in Makkah more than {4} days after the Hajj — ask your group leader).
<1>Qarn al-Manazil (As-Sayl)</1> — from Najd, Taif, UAE & most eastern flights

<1>Qiran</1> — one ihram for both (<2>Labbayk Allahumma 'Umratan wa Hajjan</2>): arrival tawaf and sa'i, then you stay in ihram until the {1}th — what the Prophet ﷺ himself did because he had his hady with him (Bukhari {2}). <3>Hady owed.</3> The majority: one sa'i covers both; Hanafis: a Qarin does two.
<1>Rawdah visit permit</1> (Masjid an-Nabawi) — free but limited; slots open only a short time ahead, so check Nusuk as your dates approach and book as soon as they open

<1>Rida (upper cloth):</1> drape it over both shoulders like a shawl, covering the back and chest; ends hang in front. For the arrival tawaf, pass it under the right arm (idtiba') (Hanafis and Shafi'is: also in a later tawaf followed by sa'i) — then cover both shoulders again before praying.

<1>Stoning:</1> go at night when the bridge is quieter (most scholars allow it for those who could not go earlier; the Hanbali school: the next day after midday), or <2>delegate</2> it to someone who has stoned for themselves (permitted by all four schools, al-Mughni — Ibn Majah {1} has a weak chain, its meaning is accepted; Malikis add a dam for the one unable).

<1>Tamattu'</1> — ihram for Umrah at the miqat (<2>Labbayk Allahumma 'Umrah</2>), finish it, live normally in Makkah, then ihram again for Hajj on the {1}th. The Prophet ﷺ ordered his companions without a sacrificial animal to do this (Bukhari {2}) and said he would have done it himself had he not brought his hady (Bukhari {3}). <3>Hady owed.</3> The choice of almost every package, and this app's default.

<1>Tawaf & sa'i:</1> a wheelchair, the electric carts and the upper floors are fully valid (Bukhari {1}); wheelchairs are available free or for rent at official points around the Haram (ask the Haram staff) — never pay touts.
<1>Taxis / Uber / Careem</1> — plentiful; agree street-taxi fares before riding.

<1>Too ill to continue?</1> With the conditional intention (ishtirat) made at the miqat, the Shafi'is and Hanbalis hold you leave ihram with nothing owed (Bukhari {1}); the Hanafis and Malikis do not give the condition this effect. Without it, the schools differ — the Hanafis treat illness as being prevented, so the hady of Quran {2} applies, while the majority say you stay in ihram until you can complete the rites — ask a scholar through your group leader.

<1>When:</1> the {1}th after stoning is the sunnah. The Hanafis, Malikis and the Hanbali school allow it until sunset on the {2}th; some Hanbalis and many later scholars allow the {3}th too, and the Shafi'is set no last day — the {4}th–{5}th is valid for everyone. "All of Mina is a place of sacrifice" (Abu Dawud {6}).

<1>Which?</1> Arriving days before the {1}th: Tamattu' — easier on the body and the family, and what the Prophet ﷺ wished for himself. Arriving on the {2}th or {3}th straight into the rites: Qiran or Ifrad spare you a second ihram. Whatever you said at the miqat is what you are — the app asks you at the halq step of your Umrah.
<1>Yalamlam</1> — from Yemen & the south
<1>eSIM or local SIM</1> (STC, Mobily, Zain) at the airport — data is cheap and essential.
<1>{1} & {2} · Tashriq</1> — after midday stone the three jamarat in order ({3} each, dua after the first two); nights in Mina; leave Mina before sunset on the {4}th, or stay.

<1>{1} Dhul Hijjah · Tarwiyah</1> — ihram for Hajj from your hotel (Tamattu'), then Mina; Dhuhr to Fajr prayed there, shortened not combined (Bukhari {2}, {3}) — the Malikis shorten here regardless, as a rite of Hajj, and so do many later scholars (Ibn Taymiyyah, Ibn Baz); the Hanafis ({4}+ days in Makkah before the {5}th) and the Shafi'is ({6} full days, not counting the days of arrival and departure) treat shortening as for travellers only, count you a resident and pray four rakahs here — though the Shafi'is let you shorten from the moment you leave Makkah for Mina if you will set off for home after the rites without staying another {7} full days in Makkah (al-Majmu' {8}/{9}; Nihayat al-Muhtaj {10}/{11}); the Hanbali school has you pray four here only if you will stay on in Makkah for more than {12} days after the Hajj; ask your group leader which your group follows.

<1>{1} · Arafah</1> — after sunrise to Arafah; Dhuhr + Asr together at Dhuhr; stand in dua until sunset — "Hajj is Arafah" (Tirmidhi {2}). After sunset to Muzdalifah: Maghrib + Isha together, sleep, Fajr, dhikr, leave before sunrise (the weak after midnight).
<1>{1} · Yawm an-Nahr</1> — stone Jamrat al-Aqabah ({2} pebbles), hady, shave or trim→first tahallul; tawaf al-ifadah + sa'i→second tahallul; night in Mina.
<1>{1}</1> — if you stayed: stone again after midday, then leave.
A <1>dam</1> for a missed wajib is a separate sheep — see the fiqh Q&A.

A mistake made through genuine forgetfulness or ignorance carries no sin; whether a fidyah is still owed differs between the schools (most say it is for cutting hair or nails) — ask a scholar. Showering (unscented), changing ihram garments, belts, glasses, watches, umbrellas — all fine.
Aishah (RA): "Some of us assumed ihram for Umrah only, some for both Hajj and Umrah, and others for Hajj only" (Bukhari {1}). All three are valid; the difference is how Umrah and Hajj are joined.
Arguing, foul language & sin (Quran {1})
Arrive {1}–{2} min before prayer for a spot inside — gates close when full.
Believing each tawaf round has a fixed dua — none are prescribed; only "Rabbana atina…" between the Yamani corner and Black Stone is sunnah.
Currency: <1>Saudi Riyal (SAR)</1>. Cards & Apple Pay widely accepted; carry some cash.
Cutting hair or nails

Cutting only a few strands for taqsir — the Shafi'is accept three hairs as the minimum, but the Hanafis require at least a quarter of the head and the Malikis and Hanbalis the whole head, so trim from all around the head to be valid for everyone; halq carries greater reward for men.
Cutting through Hijr Isma'il (the semicircle by the Kaaba) — it is part of the House, so any round that passes inside it must be repeated.
Drink Zamzam constantly and pace yourself — it's a marathon of worship, not a sprint.
Easiest tawaf: <1>late night to pre-Fajr</1>. Hardest: after Isha and around Jumu'ah.
Hajj was legislated with the weak in mind: "the jihad of the elderly, the young, the weak and women is Hajj and Umrah" (Nasai {1}). Use what is permitted, without guilt.
Hotels beyond walking distance run free Haram shuttles — ask reception.
Hunting land game (Quran {1}–{2}) — and inside the Haram, hunting or cutting its plants is forbidden to everyone, in ihram or not (Bukhari {3})
Intimacy and anything leading to it
Keep small notes for sadaqah, barbers (agree the price first — shops right by the Haram charge more) and water.
Kissing the Yamani corner — it is touched, not kissed; the Black Stone is kissed only if easily reached.
Loud group dhikr in tawaf — it disturbs others; recite individually.
Marriage contracts or proposals (the majority; the Hanafis hold a contract made in ihram valid)
Men: stitched fitted clothing, covering the head
Must-have apps: <1>Nusuk</1>, <2>Haramain Rail</2>, <3>Careem/Uber</3>, a prayer-times app — and this one
Never push at the Black Stone — pointing to it from afar with a takbir is the sunnah when it cannot be reached (Bukhari {1}).

Once in ihram, avoid these until you come out of ihram — in Umrah, after the cut; in Hajj, most of them lift at the first release on the {1}th, while intimacy (and, in some schools, the marriage contract and hunting) waits until tawaf al-ifadah:

Performing your Umrah also needs a <1>free Umrah permit</1> (a date-and-time slot) issued in Nusuk — check it shows in the app before you go to the Haram in ihram. General prayer in both Harams needs <2>no permit</2>. Rules change by season, so check the Nusuk app before you travel and set it up with your passport details.
Perfume or scented products (body or garments)
Praying with the right shoulder uncovered after tawaf — cover both shoulders for salah.
Raml in all {1} rounds — men do it in the first {2} only, in the arrival tawaf (Hanafis and Shafi'is: also in a later tawaf followed by sa'i).
